validity.researcher_notes: The citations show a real line, part of the Lower Tura to Perm to Gorky to Center system, taken into operation in 1974 to 1976 and run by Gazprom Transgaz Nizhny Novgorod. Caveat: no citation gives the length of this line alone.

fills.researcher_notes: An Interfax report of 27 December 2018 on pipeline accidents, built from Rostekhnadzor data, lists the Gorky to Center line as run by Gazprom Transgaz Nizhny Novgorod (a Gazprom subsidiary) and notes a break on 24 October 2018. The company history page, read as a Wayback capture of June 2025, lists the line among those it took into operation.

fills.researcher_notes: The company history page, read as a Wayback capture of June 2025, says the Perm to Gorky I, Perm to Gorky II and Gorky to Center lines were taken into operation in 1974 to 1976. It does not give one year for Gorky to Center, so 1974 is the start of that range.
No harvested citation gives the length of the Gorky to Center line alone. The Wikipedia article says the whole Lower Tura to Perm to Gorky to Center system is more than 1,700 km.
